13 short at two or more US firms — upstream of all of them
10 short at exactly one — this cannot tell a supply problem from one company's
13 of the 23 substances short in all three countries are short at two or more separate US firms at once. Methylphenidate at six, methylprednisolone at five.
Six companies do not independently fail at the same molecule in the same month. For these nine the supply-chain reading is evidence rather than inference.
The other ten are a single US supplier, which is also what a market with one supplier looks like. Counted separately, not folded into the headline.
US column only — France and Australia publish no firm at all, so a drug short at one US firm might be short at six French ones and this cannot see it.
